**Interviewee**: Rainless Meadow  
**Location**: Near the Old Gavril Plaza  
**Titan Observations**: Firsthand Account of Progenitor Titan  
  
Rainless Meadow was still shaken from her encounter with Greer at the time of her interview. Another lowlander, Whispers of Wind, sent the young kodan into the woods to scout while they were establishing a foothold in the ruins of Gavril. Meadow first went west to find clean water.  
  
Upon entering the westernmost swamp, she heard the titan Greer rise from his den. Meadow was able to duck into a small cave before he could identify her. Based on her description of the beast, Greer is significantly larger than any titan we've encountered on record—although our records may be sparse in that regard. Just as we've never witnessed their spawn, the size of these creatures makes me wonder if these specific titans have... Ah, I'm not sure—perhaps they've tapped into a well of power they didn't have access to before? Or, given the secluded nature of Janthir, maybe their development has been largely uninterrupted? It's challenging to draw that connection without knowing how long they've been present, however.

The former Pact commander—or wayfinder, or whatever they call themselves these days—has been seen entering the current headquarters of the Tyrian Alliance. While this individual's contributions to the world are relatively well-known and appreciated by many, some concerns have been shared about how much power an individual should be able to wield. Additional concerns have been expressed about how much influence they have on our world leaders. Should a nonstate actor be able to wine and dine with the power players? Such sequestered decisions can affect the lives of millions. It's simply not for us to say.  
  
Of even greater concern than the naysayers: a fan organization has built up around the commander's celebrity status. Some have even described it as a cult engaging in a form of hero worship. While we want to reiterate the genuine appreciation for the commander's actions, it could be dangerous to allow this practice to continue. Some are even saying that the commander has died and come back to life—which, of course, is nonsense. I'm sure the commander would agree with this statement.

Haebaragi has placed Jimin on probation until further notice. Yeongi hasn't taken to her style of rule...he and the rest of the Ministry of Purity have moved their operation to an outpost on the edge of the city. Rumor has it, Haebaragi is going to disband them—just as she disbanded the Celestial Ministry in favor of a more inclusive and open governance.

Meanwhile...we've finally reached the edge of the new city. It only took eighteen years of blood, sweat, and endless bottles of sweet pear wine (I owe Dwayna a thousand thanks that the winery in Sunjiang was salvageable).

We stopped our excavation efforts on the edge of Echovald Forest. A representative from the new Ministry of Urban Planning mapped out a wall that'll stretch from Nahpui, curve around the bay, and end here, securing the city from a possible second wave.

Minister Doh Taelin, Ministry of Archives, 1747 CC

While envoys have reached various groups of quaggan and largos, it's hard to determine the impact that the death of the water dragon has had on their cultures or the sea as a whole. The largos have always been difficult to reach out to, and for now, at least, the alliance has been informed that the Tethyos Houses are not open to cooperation. The ward has at least one largos within its ranks who has expressed an eagerness to support this cause. It may be worth considering sending one of their own out to see if she can make better headway.  
  
We'd hoped to have better luck with the deep-sea quaggan, but our envoys were rebuffed once again. Truthfully, this is unexpected for that species; they are usually quite eager to volunteer themselves to larger causes. Whatever is going on down there must be quite serious and should not be ignored.  
  
Some asura from the colleges, ward members, and engineers from Xunlai Jade have proposed an initiative to outfit the Pact's submarines with better tech and magic, but they seem to be busier arguing with each other than making legitimate progress on that front. Alliance intervention is recommended.
